paragraphs: One-sentence judgment: bioinformatics technicians are not operators who just click buttons following a procedure, but a support position that translates the data needs of researchers into runnable queries and analyses, processes biological data into searchable databases, and maintains the state of tools and data to reproducibility: enter and retrieve information from structural databases and protein sequence motif databases and mutation databases and genomic databases or gene expression databases according to data needs, analyze or manipulate bioinformatics data with software packages and statistical applications or data mining techniques, write computer programs or scripts to query databases, develop or maintain applications that process biological data into searchable databases, design or implement web-based tools to query large biological databases, monitor database performance and carry out necessary maintenance and upgrades and repairs, record all changes and problems in the database, perform quality analysis on input data and output results, carry out routine system administration such as troubleshooting and backup and upgrades, test new or updated software or tools and give feedback to developers, and train researchers in using the databases; people who only want ready-made conclusions and are unwilling to trace data sources and parameters and versions, unwilling to handle biological and human-related data according to data and privacy rules, and unwilling to stop, review and report first when data are anomalous or beyond authorization are not suited to it.

Signals to keep exploring: you are willing to trace a query or analysis result back to the original data and the script and tool version; you can travel back and forth among databases and scripts and data and documentation over the long term and keep things reproducible; when data items are missing or a tool errors out or results do not match expectations you are willing to review first and record truthfully rather than picking the results that are usable; you are willing to stop and report first when human genetic resources and personal information are involved or your data authorization is exceeded.

Conditions for pausing your investment first: you have not yet completed, under any supervised condition, one full closed loop of requirements confirmation, data retrieval and validation, running tools and analysis, result review, reproducible records, and delivery and support, or you can only explain your interest by liking biology or knowing how to code; nor should you treat being able to use one bioinformatics software package or write a script as proof that you can independently decide the scope of data acquisition or independently decide submissions of human-related data and public database submissions. The acquisition and use and sharing and submission of biological and human-related data must be carried out in accordance with the applicable jurisdiction and competent authorities and institutional ethics and authorization requirements and records must be retained; this page does not provide any practice for circumventing regulation.

On that basis this page publishes the wage and employment and industry fields in the parent occupation 15-2099.00 scope with labels at every occurrence, and does not treat parent occupation values as a standalone scope for this occupation or as an income promise. Education, vocational training, industry certification, employer hiring and position authorization, database and system and data authority, and the requirements of the applicable jurisdiction for human genetic resources and personal information are different states and must be verified item by item according to employer and position and jurisdiction. On the mainland China side, no nationally comparable wage scope corresponding one-to-one to this occupation was established in this round, and this page publishes no mainland China wage figures and only retains a visible gap marker.

One sentence: this is a technical support position centered on data retrieval and quality analysis, script and database and tool maintenance, and collaboration and training; the core is reproducible data and scripts and results, not the imagination of biology; its U.S. wage and employment and industry data fall under the parent occupation 15-2099.00 scope with labels at every occurrence; on the mainland China side no nationally comparable wage scope corresponding one-to-one to this occupation was obtained, and this page publishes no mainland China wage figures and visibly marks the gap as insufficient evidence.

The work of bioinformatics technicians can be divided into three categories: data extraction and quality analysis (enter and retrieve information from structural databases and protein sequence motif databases and mutation databases and genomic databases or gene expression databases according to research needs; analyze or manipulate bioinformatics data with software packages and statistical applications or data mining techniques; perform quality analysis on input data and output results; develop or apply data mining and machine learning algorithms; and package and submit bioinformatics data to public repositories); script and database and tool maintenance (write computer programs or scripts to query databases; develop or maintain applications that process biological data into searchable databases; extend existing software programs and web-based interactive tools or database queries according to sequence management and analysis needs; design or implement web-based tools to query large biological databases; monitor database performance and carry out necessary maintenance and upgrades and repairs; record all changes and modifications and problems in the database; carry out routine system administration functions such as troubleshooting and backup and upgrades; test new or updated software or tools and give feedback to developers); and collaboration and training and documentation (consult with researchers and clinical staff or information technology staff to determine data needs and programming requirements and assist database-related research activities; consult with database users about project timelines and changes; write data management or error checking programs and user manuals; train bioinformatics staff or researchers in using databases; participate in the preparation of reports or scientific publications; and stay informed about new and emerging computational methods and technologies). What the three categories share is writing data sources and script and tool versions clearly, rather than taking the desired results first and adding the conditions afterwards.

The current task set has 19 items, 10 core and 9 supplemental; 18 items have importance scores and one item, designing web query tools, is not scored. There are 41 work activities, 16 detailed activities and 57 context items. The higher work activities are using computers 98 and analyzing/processing information 94 and getting information 90; the highest-importance tasks differ from the supplemental/core classification, and it cannot be inferred from the scores that every person carries out all tasks.

Run tools and analyze | Make the results testable | Analyze or manipulate bioinformatics data with software packages or statistical applications or data mining techniques, or develop and apply data mining and machine learning algorithms, implemented and run in a reproducible way.

Script and database maintenance | Make the tools dependable | Write query scripts and develop or maintain biological data applications, monitor database performance and carry out maintenance and upgrades and repairs, and truthfully record all changes and problems in the database.

Review and delivery and support | Make the results transferable | Review and rerun anomalies and inconsistencies first, keep parameters and versions and run records, write data management and error checking programs and user manuals, and provide support to researchers and database users.

Compliance and escalation | Stop risks early | When human genetic resources and personal information and ethical matters are involved or something is beyond your authorization, report and hand over according to the authorization chain and do not handle it on your own.

The basis for comparison is the official occupation description of O*NET 15-2099.01 and the list of related occupations on the O*NET page (Bioinformatics Scientists, Biological Technicians, Cytogenetic Technologists, Data Scientists, Database Administrators, Database Architects, Health Information Technologists and Medical Registrars, Medical and Clinical Laboratory Technologists, Medical Records Specialists, Social Science Research Assistants, Statistical Assistants, Bioengineers and Biomedical Engineers, Clinical Data Managers, Statisticians, Biostatisticians, Computer and Information Research Scientists, Geographic Information Systems Technologists and Technicians, Molecular and Cellular Biologists, Natural Sciences Managers and others), as well as the adjacent occupation relationships noted in the routing materials; an adjacent relationship only indicates proximity of duties and does not mean that qualifications, authorization or positions are interchangeable.

The table below compares bioinformatics technicians with five adjacent directions on the same set of dimensions: occupational direction, core work and outputs, key differences, and which choice suits each preference.

Bioinformatics scientists take question and hypothesis setting and method and statistical inference as their main object and decide the computational strategy at the level of the research question; bioinformatics technicians take running and maintaining tools and databases according to established requirements as their main object and deliver data and scripts and support according to the requirements given by the research side and the platform.

If you would rather define research questions and choose methods and make statistical inferences, compare bioinformatics scientists first; if you would rather maintain tools and databases according to requirements and support users, then this occupation suits you.
Complete statistical inference and conclusion publication, with outputs mainly in analysis methods and conclusions and papers.
Bioinformatics technicians and bioinformatics scientists

Data scientists take broader business data and modeling and product delivery as their main object and are driven by business goals in commercial and industrial contexts; bioinformatics technicians take biological data and databases and tool support as their main object and need to understand the format and source and quality requirements of biological data.

If you would rather do business data and modeling and product delivery, compare data scientists first; if you would rather maintain databases and tools around biological data, then this occupation suits you.
Complete business data modeling and delivery, with outputs mainly in models and metrics and business reports.
Bioinformatics technicians and data scientists

Database administrators take the availability and performance and security and backup of general databases as their main duty and do not focus on the semantics of biological data; bioinformatics technicians need to understand the structure and application context of biological data at the same time.

If you would rather do the availability and performance and security management of general databases, compare database administrators first; if you would rather apply database capabilities to biological data, then this occupation suits you.
Complete database availability and performance and security management, with outputs mainly in database operations and security and backup records.
Bioinformatics technicians and database administrators

Biological technicians take laboratory samples and experimental operations as their main duty and produce mainly wet-lab data; bioinformatics technicians take computing and data and tools as their main object and do not directly take on wet-lab operations.
If you would rather do laboratory samples and experimental operations, compare biological technicians first; if you would rather do data and script and tool support, then this occupation suits you.
Complete experimental operations and sample handling, with outputs mainly in experimental data and records.
Bioinformatics technicians and biological technicians

If you would rather do data organization and statistical support, compare statistical assistants first; if you would rather do biological data and tools and databases, then this occupation suits you.
Complete data organization and statistical support, with outputs mainly in datasets and statistical summaries.
Bioinformatics technicians and statistical assistants

Natural sciences managers take research organization and personnel and budget and compliance management as their main duty and do not directly take on day-to-day data and tool maintenance; bioinformatics technicians take data and scripts and databases and support as their main object.

entries.answer: Apply the principles and methods of bioinformatics to assist scientists: perform quality analysis on input data and on the analyses or predictions obtained; enter and retrieve information from structural databases and protein sequence motif databases and mutation databases and genomic databases or gene expression databases according to research needs; analyze or manipulate bioinformatics data using software packages or statistical applications or data mining techniques; write computer programs or scripts to query databases; develop or maintain applications that process biological data into searchable databases; extend existing software programs and web-based interactive tools or database queries according to sequence management and analysis needs; design or implement web-based tools to query large biological databases; monitor database performance and carry out maintenance and upgrades and repairs; record all changes and problems in the database; carry out routine system administration functions such as troubleshooting and backup and upgrades; test new or updated software or tools and give feedback to developers; consult with researchers and clinical staff or information technology staff to determine data needs and programming requirements; write data management or error checking programs and user manuals; train bioinformatics staff or researchers in using databases; participate in the preparation of reports or scientific publications; and package and submit bioinformatics data to public repositories.

entries.answer: Key risks include crossing data acquisition and operation authorization boundaries, privacy and compliance risks for human-related data, non-reproducible scripts and processes and conclusions, tool output and automatically generated scripts being treated as conclusions, long screen hours and repetitive actions and load, and external data submission and openness beyond authorization; the control approach is to work first within the authorized data and systems and ethics scope and carry out risk identification, handle human-related data according to procedure and retain records, truthfully record data and scripts and parameters and versions and database changes, deliver results and submit data within the authorized scope, and stop and escalate when beyond authorization or when anomalies are found.

hero.quick_answer: Bioinformatics technicians apply the principles and methods of bioinformatics to assist scientists: provide support in areas such as pharmaceuticals and medical technology or biotechnology or computational biology or proteomics or computer information science or biology and medical informatics, and apply bioinformatics tools to visualize and analyze or manipulate or interpret molecular data; common work includes entering and retrieving information from structural databases and protein sequence motif databases and mutation databases and genomic databases or gene expression databases according to research needs, analyzing or manipulating bioinformatics data using software packages or statistical applications or data mining techniques, performing quality analysis on input data and on the analyses or predictions obtained, writing computer programs or scripts to query databases, developing or maintaining applications that process biological data into searchable databases, extending existing software programs and web-based interactive tools or database queries according to sequence management and analysis needs, designing or implementing web-based tools to query large biological databases, monitoring database performance and carrying out maintenance and upgrades and repairs, recording all changes and problems in the database, carrying out routine system administration functions such as troubleshooting and backup and upgrades, developing or applying data mining and machine learning algorithms, testing new or updated software or tools and giving feedback to developers, consulting with researchers and clinical staff or information technology staff to determine data needs and programming requirements, writing data management or error checking programs and user manuals, training bioinformatics staff or researchers in using databases, participating in the preparation of reports or scientific publications, and packaging and submitting bioinformatics data to public repositories; their work does not equal the final determination of research conclusions or approval for human-related data and public repository submission, nor does it replace the regulatory requirements of the applicable jurisdiction and competent authorities and institutional ethics and management rules for human genetic resources and personal information and biological data management, and it stops and escalates when data sources are non-compliant, when situations requiring specific approval such as human-related data and cross-border transmission are involved, or when anomalous results are found or situations beyond one's authorization are involved.
